title: Record invariants and operations
goal: Protect identifier uniqueness and the state sequence by checking operation conditions before changing a record.

prerequisites.text: Know records, lookups in arrays of records and conditional state changes.
Be able to pass an object's address and check preconditions before writing to it.

terms.title: Invariant
terms.definition: A property of a valid store that holds before and after each command. Here IDs are unique and count does not exceed capacity. A rejected operation leaves the store unchanged.

terms.title: Capacity
terms.definition: The number of available slots. count includes only occupied slots.

terms.title: Precondition
terms.definition: A condition checked before changing state. For example, an added identifier must not already be present.

sections.title: Validate first, then update
paragraphs: The operation starts with a valid store. A request needs a unique identifier and the sequence new → active → done. An invalid command must preserve the previous record.
Separate checking from writing. First decide whether the change is valid. Assign only in the success branch. For insertion, store count and capacity separately.

Check order affects the diagnostic result. If the store is full and the ID already exists, this contract reports duplicate because it checks the ID before capacity. A test can then explain each rejection unambiguously.

sections.title: A storage tray advances one state at a time
paragraphs: Tray 41 is in RECEIVED. The first attempt tries to store it immediately. Predict what the program prints after each attempt.
steps: Check RECEIVED → STORED. It is disallowed, so move_tray returns 0 without storing next.
Print the state after rejection. Code 1 remains unchanged.
The next attempt RECEIVED → CHECKED is allowed. Only then does the state change to 2.

sections.title: Locate and check the defect
paragraphs: The Clang message is a pointer for current.state means that current is a pointer. Use current->state to access a member through it. In the worked example main passes move_tray the address &tray of a live object. The function checks the state transition before writing.
If adding 101 reports ok and the final line contains ID 101 twice, compare the array before and after that operation. The existing-key check is missing even if count still fits the capacity.

sections.title: Change, predict and check
paragraphs: Move the allowed attempt to the beginning. Explain the order: after RECEIVED → CHECKED, CHECKED → STORED is now valid.

In the practice, treat the two commands as a sequence. A malformed line is rejected before either command. With a correctly parsed line, the first successful operation remains applied even if the second is rejected.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Review the language constructs used in the worked example.

selfcheck.prompt: Which state is printed after the first attempt in the example?
feedback: The record is preserved when the transition is rejected.
3 cannot be stored from the initial state.

selfcheck.prompt: What should an attempt to add existing ID 101 to a full array report under this contract?
feedback: Capacity is checked after the identifier.
Reject the duplicate first. The store stays the same.
Success would violate uniqueness and capacity.

selfcheck.prompt: The first command moves 101 from 1 to 2. The second tries to move closed 203 from 3 back to 2. Which two results should appear, and why is the first update retained?
selfcheck.feedback: ok and denied. Commands are checked and applied independently in order. The second command does not roll back the first.

practice.title: Two commands for a request queue
practice.task: A store with capacity 3 initially contains 101:1 and 203:2. The first line, up to 63 bytes, contains exactly two triples of operation, ID and state. Operation 1 inserts a request only in state 1. Operation 2 advances an existing request along 1 → 2 → 3. IDs are 1–9999. A malformed line, an operation code outside 1/2, or values outside input bounds reject the entire line as invalid. The input state field accepts 0–9 syntactically; allowed operation states are 1, 2 and 3. An unknown operation state or insertion outside state 1 yields invalid for that command. Insertion checks duplicate before full. An update yields missing for an absent record and denied for a forbidden transition. Success yields ok. For a correctly parsed line print both command results followed by the records as id:state separated by spaces in array order. Complete apply by checking for an existing identifier before testing capacity.

cases.label: Two transitions on the same record

criteria: A duplicate identifier and an unknown record preserve the original snapshot. A valid insertion fills the last slot.
Transitions 1 → 2 and 2 → 3 are allowed; repeating or skipping is rejected. A command sees the result of the preceding one.
Checks run before a write. On a malformed line neither command is applied.
practice.hint: The starter already calls lookup. In the insert branch return duplicate if request != NULL before testing capacity. Construct a check in which both rejection reasons apply.

steps.action: Enter one line, 1 321 1 1 321 1, and run the starter. Record both command results and the final records.
steps.why: Both commands run together. The first fills the last slot, and the second must recognize the same ID.
steps.expected: The starter prints ok, then full, then 101:1 203:2 321:1.

steps.action: Add the existing-ID check. Repeat that input, then test 1 101 1 2 999 2.
steps.why: Check the order of the two rejection rules and verify the records after both rejected commands.
steps.expected: The first input gives ok, duplicate and the same snapshot with ID 321. The second gives duplicate, missing and 101:1 203:2.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: Write two commands that move the same record from 1 to 3 through allowed intermediate steps. Reverse the commands and predict where the contract rejects a move.
criteria: 2 101 2 2 101 3 yields ok, ok and 101:3 203:2. Reversing order yields denied, ok and 101:2 203:2.
